data.body:
Implemented and pushed as Gerrit change 2620
(https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2620). NOT closed, and NO terraform
apply or plan was run — the change lands the IaC and its offline guards only.

## Plan review
PASS, 0 blocking / 2 advisory, signed at head_sha 69cd2b9e15aa6030e5d92c43357b8059a3f5c616
(current origin/main), manifest `rebar-version: 0.13.1 (69cd2b9e15aa)` — i.e. the worktree
build, not a stale global install. `review-plan --status` re-reports `certified`.

Both advisories were honoured in the implementation without touching the description (which
would have invalidated the attestation):
- P6 ac-quality — 3 AC lines bundle deliverables with "and". Noted; each bundled clause has
  its own assertion in the test module, so nothing is unverified.
- G6 — the fourth marker quadrant (declaration absent + proof PRESENT) was unspecified.
  Resolved explicitly as today's behaviour and pinned by
  `test_proof_without_declaration_also_admits`.

## What was config vs. what needed code

`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` did make most of it configuration, as the epic comment predicted:
relocation is a gp3 volume + a UUID fstab mount + `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`/`TMPDIR` on the
review-bot service + a bind mount. Note it takes BOTH env vars — `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` moves
the content-addressed store, but the voter's per-review clone is a plain
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reviewbot-")` and follows `TMPDIR`. That clone is the
one whose bytes scale linearly with concurrency, so setting only the first is half a fix.

What `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` could NOT do is the refusal, and the gap is subtle enough to be
worth recording. S6 already fails closed on an `OSError` from the store root, but an
unmounted volume raises nothing: a mount point whose volume is absent is an ordinary,
writable, EMPTY directory, so `store_root()`'s `mkdir(parents=True)` recreates the store on
root and every gate keeps working — silently — on the disk this epic exists to protect.

Two marker files on two DIFFERENT filesystems make the states decidable:
`/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required` (root, survives an unmount — the declaration) and
`/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted` (the volume, vanishes with it — the
proof). Only declaration-present + proof-absent refuses, raising S6's existing
`GateScratchUnavailableError` BEFORE `_slot_dir()` touches the store. Every other combination
is today's behaviour, so the guard is opt-in by provisioning rather than by rebar version.

Files rather than a knob was deliberate: a `REBAR_*` literal or a `[snapshot]` key would be a
new mechanism, and `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports `active=682 new=0 increased=0`.
The check also runs ahead of the concurrency cap's `0` off-switch and the `fcntl` disarm — a
host that turned the counter off did not thereby consent to losing its scratch volume.

The container binds `/var/lib/rebar` (the mount's PARENT), not the mount point: bind only the
mount point and the container sees an empty directory in both states and the guard can never
fire. A plain host bind, not an `external:` volume, so `config-check.sh` check 5's
compose-up pairing is untouched (`--print-volumes` output unchanged).

## Other notes for S2-S5

- `user_data.sh`'s NVMe-by-volume-id resolution is now ONE function with two callers
  (`resolve_ebs_device` / `mount_ebs_volume`) rather than a second inline copy. The by-id
  symlink fallback exists because the nvme-cli path has been observed to miss; a copy that
  lacked it fails on exactly the boot the fallback was added for.
- `mount -a` does NOT prove a mount happened — a `nofail` entry is skipped quietly — so the
  scratch mount is asserted with `mountpoint -q` and exits non-zero.
- TWO alarms, per the 3e92 precedent: `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high` (disk_used_percent,
  mount dimension) and `rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` (a 1/0 heartbeat). A volume that failed
  to mount reads 0% used — perfectly healthy — while every gate refuses, so the first alarm
  structurally cannot answer for the second. Both are `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` and
  are now pinned BY NAME in `test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`'s watched set, which is ADR
  0112's standing obligation not to regress bug 3276's missing-data fix by copy-paste.
  Anti-vacuity floors raised 19 -> 21 and 14 -> 16.
- `observability.sh` §2e decides mountedness from the SAME proof marker the refusal reads,
  not from `mountpoint` — a bind mount is a mount point inside a container whether or not the
  host volume is mounted underneath, and monitoring that disagrees with enforcement is worse
  than none. Pinned by `test_the_probe_reads_the_same_marker_the_gate_refusal_reads`.
- Sizing: 50 GiB default, `var.gate_scratch_volume_size_gb`. Basis is the ADR's 3.6 G of
  gate/investigation scratch in the 28 G root working set, against S6's cap of 4 concurrent
  gates; 50 GiB leaves ~42 GiB below the 85% alarm.
- No `prevent_destroy` and no DLM schedule, deliberately: the contents are rebuildable, and
  both runbooks say so, because during an incident that is the difference between clearing
  the volume and treating it as data.

## Verification (all from the worktree venv)

`make lint` exit 0; `make typecheck` "Success: no issues found in 755 source files";
`terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform` clean; `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform
validate` "The configuration is valid" (after `init -backend=false`, which touches no AWS
state). The three gates `make lint` does not cover — `test_mechanism_delta.py`,
`test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`, `test_api_surface_gate.py` — 54 passed, run after
`git add`. Broader sweep of the infra/compose/review-bot-adjacent suites plus all of
`tests/scripts/`: 1590 passed, 23 skipped.

RED-first evidence: the new `tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` was written and run
BEFORE any implementation — 12 failed / 1 passed, and the one that passed
(`test_no_declaration_means_no_assertion`) is the test that asserts today's unchanged
behaviour, so its passing was the correct RED result.
